les: Van die son tot op jou bord
kaps_punt: Energie van die Son: energie word oorgedra van die Son, na plante, na diere in 'n volgorde wat bekend is as 'n energie-/voedselketting

items.bewering: Jy weet al dat 'n bok die blare van 'n plant vreet.
items.bron: MSD Veterinary Manual, 'Herbage and browse utilization in goats' (msdvetmanual.com): goats prefer browse, the leaves and twigs of trees and shrubs, over grass; Frontiers in Veterinary Science 2022 (doi 10.3389/fvets.2022.1032631): goats are classed as browsers and grazers.

items.bewering: Jy weet ook dat daardie plant sy kos met die son se lig maak.
items.bron: National Geographic Education, 'Energy flow' (education.nationalgeographic.org): producers capture the sun's energy through photosynthesis; Nagwa explainer 'Respiration in plants' and docbrown.info: light energy is converted to chemical energy in glucose.

items.bewering: Die son staan eerste, die plant tweede en die bok laaste.
items.bron: 'eerste' is a position in this three-link chain, not a claim about history. It matches the order the CAPS bullet itself gives (Son, plante, diere), as quoted in the lesson's kaps_punt, and the WCED ePortal/CapeNature CAPS-aligned Gr 4 energy lesson plan (capenature.co.za): energy goes from the sun to plants, then to animals.

items.bewering: Elke skakel gee 'n deel van die energie aan die volgende skakel aan.
items.bron: Mapping checked: a 'ketting' of 'skakels' that each pass on PART of the energy holds. Only some of the energy goes to the next level (about 10% on average, 5-20%) because of respiration and waste (JoVE 'Trophic efficiency'; albert.io AP Biology review). The sun also gives a plant only a small part of its output, so 'n deel holds for the first link too. The last link has no next link, and 'elke' plainly covers only links that have one, so this does not mislead.

items.bewering: So 'n ry noem ons 'n energieketting, en 'n voedselketting is dieselfde ding.
items.bron: The CAPS Gr 4 bullet quoted in the lesson's kaps_punt calls the sequence an 'energie-/voedselketting', so the curriculum treats the two as one. The NECT Gr 4 Term 3 tracker search snippet gives the same wording ('a sequence known as an energy chain/ food chain'); the document was not opened. Note for a human, not a fault: general sources often start a food chain at the producer (weet.co.za, 'Voedselketting'), not at the sun. The lesson follows CAPS here, and its glossary entry limits the sun-first rule to 'in hierdie les'.

items.bewering: 'n Plant het lig nodig om kos te maak, en buite kom daardie lig van die son.
items.blok: Hoekom die son heel eerste staan
items.bron: National Geographic Education 'Energy flow': the sun is the ultimate source of energy for most ecosystems, captured by producers through photosynthesis; docbrown.info: a plant cannot photosynthesise at night. 'buite' correctly limits this to outdoor plants.

items.bewering: Die son maak sy eie lig en kry dit nie by 'n ander skakel nie.
items.blok: Hoekom die son heel eerste staan
items.bron: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio 'Origin of Light' (svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/11084) and NASA StarChild: the Sun makes its light by nuclear fusion in its core.

items.bewering: In elke ketting in hierdie les staan die son dus heel eerste. (also the heading 'Hoekom die son heel eerste staan')
items.blok: Hoekom die son heel eerste staan
items.bron: Checked inside the lesson: all four chains in 'Vier kettings in volgorde' and the chains in the study text start with the sun. The claim is limited to 'hierdie les', so it does not say that all food chains everywhere start with the sun, which would be false for chemosynthetic chains such as deep-sea vents.

items.bewering: Die son se lig val heeldag op die groen blare van die plant. Die blare vang daardie lig op en maak kos daarmee.
items.blok: Wat die plant met die lig doen
items.bron: Nagwa 'Respiration in plants'; docbrown.info photosynthesis pages: leaves take in light and use it to make glucose. 'heeldag' means during the day, which is a fair description and not a claim about night.

items.bewering: Die plant maak die kos, maar die energie kom van die son. Die plant verander die son se lig in die energie wat in sy kos gebêre word.
items.blok: Wat die plant met die lig doen
items.bron: RevisionDojo IB notes 'Flow of chemical energy through food chains' and docbrown.info: photosynthesis turns light energy into chemical energy, which is stored in glucose and starch.

items.bewering: Die plant gebruik self eers van daardie kos om te groei. As 'n dier die plant eet, kry die dier van daardie gebêre energie.
items.blok: Wat die plant met die lig doen
items.bron: TutorChase IGCSE 'How are carbohydrates used by plants for growth'; Nagwa 'Respiration in plants': glucose is used for respiration and as building material for growth. National Geographic Education 'Energy flow': herbivores get energy by eating producers.

items.bewering: 'n Bok kan nie sy eie kos maak soos 'n plant nie. Hy moet dit gaan haal deur die plant se blare te vreet. So kry die bok 'n deel van die plant se energie.
items.blok: Die dier kry dit deur te eet
items.bron: National Geographic Education 'Energy flow': consumers cannot make their own food and get energy by eating; MSD Veterinary Manual: goats eat leaves (browse); JoVE 'Trophic efficiency': only part of the energy passes to the next level.

items.bewering: 'n Luiperd vang daardie bok later en kry net 'n deel van die bok se energie.
items.blok: Die dier kry dit deur te eet
items.bron: Durham University scat and camera-trap study of leopards on Namaqualand small-livestock farms (dro.dur.ac.uk/16137, Constant et al.): goats (Capra hircus) were the largest share of leopard diet by biomass. Cape Leopard Trust 'Conflict' page (capeleopard.org.za/research/conflict): leopards kill goats in South Africa. 'net 'n deel': JoVE 'Trophic efficiency'.

items.bewering: Dit is veral omdat elke plant of dier wat geëet word, self van sy energie gebruik om te lewe. Die bok gebruik dit byvoorbeeld om rond te loop en warm te bly. Daardie energie gaan as hitte uit sy lyf weg.
items.blok: Die dier kry dit deur te eet
items.bron: Macmillan Life 11e, key concept 57.3 (digfir-published.macmillanusa.com/life11e/life11e_ch57_12.html): net production efficiency is about 3.1% for large mammals, so nearly all the energy a mammal takes in goes to respiration and not to body tissue. JoVE 'Production efficiency' (jove.com/t/10929): endotherms spend energy keeping their body temperature up. albert.io AP Biology: respiration turns most of the energy into heat. 'veral' (mainly, not only) is right: waste and parts that are not eaten are smaller losses for an endotherm like a goat. 'elke' is right because every organism respires.

items.bewering: Die bok eet 'n plant, en die luiperd eet 'n dier.
items.blok: Die dier kry dit deur te eet
items.bron: MSD Veterinary Manual (goat herbivory); Durham Namaqualand leopard diet study (leopards are carnivores that eat hyrax, antelope and goats).

items.bewering: Jy is self 'n skakel in baie van hierdie kettings. Soms is jy die skakel net na 'n plant, soos wanneer jy 'n appel eet. Soms is jy die skakel net na 'n dier, soos wanneer jy 'n stukkie vleis eet. In albei gevalle het die energie by die son begin.
items.bron: CapeNature/WCED CAPS-aligned Gr 4 energy lesson plan: energy goes from the sun to plants and then to animals and people; National Geographic Education 'Energy flow': consumers get energy by eating producers or other consumers. An apple is the fruit of a plant, and meat comes from an animal that ate plants (cattle eat mainly grass, Noble Research Institute 'Food requirements for different animals').

items.bewering: 'n Pyl wys na watter kant die energie beweeg, en dit geld vir elke pyl. ... Tussen twee lewende dinge loop die pyl van die ding wat geëet word na die ding wat eet. Die pyl wys dus byvoorbeeld van gras na 'n koei.
items.bron: The standard convention, in several independent teaching sources: the arrow points from the organism being eaten to the one eating it and shows the direction energy is transferred (Reforest London 'Food Chains' PDF; Warwickshire Wildlife Trust 'Make your own food chain'; Varsity Tutors 'Model food webs'). 'elke pyl' holds, including the sun-to-plant arrow, which the next sentences describe correctly.

items.bewering: Tussen die son en die plant gee die son se lig die energie. Die plant bêre daardie energie in sy kos. Die pyl wys dus van die son na die plant.
items.bron: RevisionDojo IB 'Flow of chemical energy through food chains': producers capture sunlight and store it as chemical energy; the arrow direction follows the convention above.

items.bewering: Party mense lees 'n pyl as die woord "eet" en trek hom dan andersom.
items.bron: NABT, The American Biology Teacher, May 2018, 'Food webs: implications for...' (nabt.org PDF), citing Grumbine 2012: students often get the direction of energy flow wrong. Teaching resources name the same mistakes: reading the arrow as 'who eats whom', and drawing arrows from eater to food (kuraplan.com 'Understanding food webs'; Varsity Tutors). The claim says 'party mense', which is properly limited.

items.bewering: Dan beteken die heel eerste pyl niks nie, want niemand eet die son nie.
items.bron: Logic checked against the convention above: drawn backwards and read as 'eet', the sun-plant arrow says that the plant eats the sun, which means nothing. The sun-plant arrow is the first one in the chain. 'heel eerste' is a position in the chain, not a historical first. Sun as a non-food energy source: NASA SVS 'Origin of Light'.

items.bewering: Die ketting word net een kant toe gelees en nooit weer terug nie. Hy loop van die son af weg.
items.bron: RevisionDojo 'Why matter is recycled in ecosystems but not energy' and Interesting Engineering 'Can energy be recycled in an ecosystem': energy moves one way, from the sun through the food chain, and leaves as heat; it is not cycled back. The absolutes 'net een kant toe' and 'nooit weer terug nie' are true for energy.

items.bewering: Gras groei dig op die veld waar die son heeldag skyn. 'n Koei loop tussen daardie gras rond en vreet dit op. Elke skakel van hierdie ketting staan reg voor jou oë.
items.bron: Noble Research Institute 'Food requirements for different animals': cattle eat mainly grass; Iowa Ag Literacy 'Beef Science': cattle eating grass is grazing. Grass grows in full sun, and the sun, grass and cow are all visible in a field. This is a description of a scene, not a claim that every field is dense.

items.bewering: Die son → gras → 'n koei
items.bron: Noble Research Institute; Iowa Ag Literacy (cattle eat mainly grass). The arrow direction matches the lesson's own rule in 'Wat 'n pyl beteken'.

items.bewering: Die son → gras → 'n bok → 'n luiperd
items.bron: Goats graze as well as browse (Frontiers in Veterinary Science 2022: classed as browsers and grazers; MSD Veterinary Manual: browse is preferred, grass is also eaten). Leopards eat goats in South Africa (Durham Namaqualand study; Cape Leopard Trust). The study text says the goat eats a plant's 'blare', and grass blades are leaves, so the chain does not contradict the text.

items.bewering: Die son → 'n appelboom → jy
items.bron: An apple tree photosynthesises and stores energy in its fruit, which people eat (photosynthesis sources above). It matches 'Jy is self 'n skakel' ('net na 'n plant, soos wanneer jy 'n appel eet').

items.bewering: Die son → mielies → 'n hoender → jy
items.bron: Grain SA, 'The importance of maize for poultry' (grainsa.co.za): maize makes up about 50-70% of South African poultry feed, and broilers eat about 43% of the maize used for animal feed. People eat chicken. It matches 'Jy is self 'n skakel' ('net na 'n dier').

items.bewering: Set test, the four chains read together and against the study text: each starts with the sun, has a plant second, and every arrow runs from the thing eaten to the thing that eats it.
items.bron: Checked as a set against the lesson's own statements and the sources above. All four start with the sun, as 'Hoekom die son heel eerste staan' and the energieketting glossary entry say. Every second link is a plant (gras, gras, appelboom, mielies), as 'Wat die plant met die lig doen' says. The animal after a plant is a plant-eater (koei, bok, hoender) and the animal after an animal eats meat (luiperd, jy), as 'Die bok eet 'n plant, en die luiperd eet 'n dier' says. 'jy' comes straight after a plant in chain 3 and straight after an animal in chain 4, as 'Jy is self 'n skakel' says. Chain 1 is the one used in 'Wat 'n pyl beteken' and 'Kyk na die veld self', and chain 2 is the one in 'Die dier kry dit deur te eet'. No pair of chains suggests a difference that does not exist, and no chain breaks the arrow rule. Chains of three and four links both agree with 'Elke skakel gee 'n deel ... aan'.

items.bewering: energie: Wat nodig is om iets te laat gebeur, beweeg of werk.
items.bron: Read on its own and in context. It matches the common child-level definition of energy as 'the ability to do work, or ... energy makes things happen' (Generation Genius 'Energy transfer lesson for kids'; UNC STEMIE: 'invisible power that makes things work or happen'). It is a simplification but not a false one, and it fits how the lesson uses the word (growing, walking, staying warm).

items.bewering: energieketting: Die volgorde waarin energie van skakel na skakel aangegee word. In hierdie les begin elke ketting by die son.
items.bron: Read on its own: true. It matches the CAPS wording in kaps_punt (energy passed from the Sun to plants to animals in a sequence). The second sentence keeps the sun-first rule to this lesson, so the entry does not claim that every chain everywhere starts with the sun.

items.bewering: skakel: Een van die dinge wat in 'n ketting agter mekaar staan.
items.bron: Read on its own: this is the ordinary meaning of a chain link, and it maps correctly onto the lesson. 'dinge' (things) and not 'lewende dinge' (living things) correctly lets the sun count as a link, which the lesson does ('Die son ... kry dit nie by 'n ander skakel nie').

opsomming: Every claim in the lesson was checked against outside sources and none is false or unsure; the four chains also hold together as a set and agree with the study text, and the only thing a person may want to know is that the lesson follows CAPS in calling an energy chain and a food chain the same thing, while many general sources start a food chain at the plant rather than at the sun.
